September, 1995     Page Reply

 How to write to us...02     -
 Chris Norfolk........03    06
 Mike Dodd............07    09
 Keith Taylor.........11    16
 Miles Kinloch........19    23
 Malcolm Goodman......25    26
 George Munro.........27    30
 Ronald Raaijen.......31    33
 Peter Deane..........36    37

   PLEASE SEND YOUR TEXTFILE!
Text is accepted in any form for
OUTLETTERS: wordprocessor files
(say which),typed or handwritten
letters. However, PLEASE send us
a textfile if possible so your
letter needn't be typed again!
The easiest for us to edit are
Tasword 2 files with the right
margin set at 32 but a textfile
in ANY format is appreciated!

Please state if there should be
parts of your letter you do not
wish published but we always use
our discretion anyway. Letters
may also be edited for clarity
and length... Please ask if you
welcome direct correspondence
from other OUTLET readers and we
will publish your full address.

From Chris Norfolk, HULL

Dear Ron,

I had to send the B external
disk drive back to EEC. Nothing
has been altered or interfered
with but the Read/Write light
failed to come on. I must say it
worked OK at times but sometimes
it would not CAT the B drive,why
I don't know.

The +3 loads fine in the A drive
but as said,it would not CAT the
B drive, as this was intermitt-
ent.

I did read the instruction in
the +3 manual re:external drives
and I also got the commands
right.

This week I had problems with
the +3; I found in 48K it would
not load and save.The reason was
that the mike and ear socket
came adrift from the +3.


This has always been a problem
with most Spectrums as you may
well know; it is the cheap and
nasty 3.5" jack plugs- and the
power supply connections are
just as bad.

In the past I have made all con-
nections with phono plugs and
sockets. I found over the years
that I could be copying a press
newscast and, if any heavy
traffic went by, all was lost -
yes, the computer reset itself.


You may say,why buy  a Spectrum?
Well, the reason was it was the
first home computer that decoded
RTTY-MORSE-Slow Scan TV.  Of
course,other computers followed.
It had to come - the PC has now
taken over these plus many more.
The main reason is the speed of
the PC which is needed to decode
many of the fancy modes that are
around today.

     Best regards to all at
       the Chezron Team,

             Chris


Brian Cavers to Chris Norfolk

Thanks, Chris.

Sounds like poor connection to
the B drive. You are right about
the dodgy SAVE/LOAD connections.
Each month I set up a routine to
save all the OUTLET files to
tape from +D and reload direct
into the +3 at the same time. It
is possible to do this with some
cassette recorders by pressing
down the PLAY and PAUSE keys and
putting the saving Spectrum in
the microphone socket and the
loading Spectrum into the mike.
However, once started, I creep
away very carefully! One bump or
heavy footfall can crash it!
                          Brian

From: Mike Dodd, CARLISLE

Dear Ron,

Further to my last letter asking
for info on the +3 RS232 port,
this is a way to import and save
a SCREEN$...

10 FORMAT LPRINT "R";"U"
20 FOR F=16375 TO 23295 : REM
   this is to remove 9 bytes of
   extra code at the start
30 POKE F, CODE INKEY$ #3
40 NEXT F
50 BORDER 0 : PAUSE 0
60 SAVE "SCREEN$" SCREEN$
70 BORDER 7 : CAT
80 REM when the border colour
   changes to black, press a key
   to save


Do you know the address of Rom-
antic Robot? I sent a letter to
them at 15 Highland Close London
NW9 0LH some weeks ago but have
had no reply. I enclosed an SAE.

            Thanks,

                 Mike


Brian Cavers to Mike Dodd

Thanks, Mike.

Those first nine bytes must be
the header bytes containing info
about the file. Theoretically,it
must be possible for a machine
code program to read those bytes
for a BASIC program and load the
file via the RS232 in the same
way as a tape load.

If anyone else would like to ex-
plore this - possibly to modify
an existing tape load routine -
please write!

Incidentally, you must be able
to use your method to load ANY
code file such as a text file.


If you save a CODE file of known
length you should be able to ex-
amine the first nine bytes to
see which holds the length and
the address and adjust your rou-
tine accordingly. BASIC loads in
a similar way but various system
variables need adjusting and of
course, any BASIC program doing
the loading would be wiped out
by the new BASIC so it would
have to be in machine code.

The last address I had for Rom-
antic Robot was 54 Deanscroft
Avenue, London, NW9 8EN but that
was in 1990! Does anyone know if
they are still trading?

                        Brian

From: Keith  Taylor, OLDHAM



Thanks for sending me the July
'92 Outlet (No. 59). I wonder if
you could spare me a few minutes
to go through the PFN fonts as I
am unable to get the extraction
(program not teeth - although I
spat a few!) working with my
programs.


On the same subject could you
tell me if the editor is avail-
able from yourselves, as I would
like to obtain it. I have
written to the author, but have,
to date, not received a reply.



Enclosed is a program which
encompasses a weekly shopping
list, summary of weekly income/
expenditure and limited bank
statement. Would you care to
comment on it?


Just a couple of points:


(1). It's tailored to my needs,
but by breaking in to the
program, it can be altered.


(2). If you think its worth it,
you can include it in a future
Outlet.




Finally I've included another of
my programs (INVEST). I'm having
a problem with it. Originally it
ran fine but I tinkered with it
to put in coloured lines.

Since altering it, if I input a
number below 1, it only prints
out the bottom half of the
array. I thought the fault lay
either in dim e$ or dim k$
(which I set up to keep the
array in line) but after chang-
ing them - still failure. In any
case I fail to see the relation-
ship between the amount entered
and loss of lines.

I would appreciate it if you
could look at it and help me
out. Thanks.


In Outlet No. 95 I see that Mr.
Ridout has an "end of file"
problem with LLIST. I too have
this problem. However, I doubt
if the fault lies in any REM or
CODE commands as none of my
programs use these.

I use a 12-pin dot matrix and
also a 9-pin with the same res-
ult.Also when I try to print out
the actual program, the printer
slows down and stops after a
couple of lines. If I clear it
and re-run it, it goes totally
dolally and prints total garb-
age.

I wonder whether the fault could
be in the use of tab commands in
our programs although it does
not explain the LLIST problem.

Could it be that the Spectrum +3
is not fully compatible? (For an
example you could try printing
out the "budget" I've enclosed).

Sorry I can't offer much in the
way of help.

                Keith Taylor


Brian Cavers to Keith Taylor

The BUDGET program seems OK but
I got an error. Take the program
as you sent it to me and try to
print out the BALANCE. I got a
few lines printed and then...

"variable not found 3300:1"

This turned out to be the vari-
able GGTOT which was undefined.

Apart from that I could only see
minor, nitpicking, details that
I would alter. For example, the
menu option, PRINTER leads to a
submenu SCREEN or PRINTER. I'd
make the first menu say, LIST or
VIEW BUDGET or something instead
of PRINTER.


If you can sort out that error
then send us the program again I
will put in OUTLET.

I need more details on that bug
in INVEST. Send me...

1. A precise list of "good" data
(and the corresponding input
prompt in the program)that I can
enter so I can see how it is
SUPPOSED to be - ie, what you
intended.

2. A precise list of "bad" data
I can enter and see the result.

I simply cannot see anything
wrong and I am sure it is just
because I am not understanding
what you mean.


I am beginning to think that the
+3 LLIST problem may be a hard-
ware fault. One of my +3's too
started to print garbage when I
got my new printer and I have
the horrible feeling I may have
removed the printer lead while
the +3 was switched on. This
should in theory be safe but you
never know. Perhaps a component
has been damaged or perhaps it
is just a bad printer lead.

Are you able to LPRINT? eg, if
you enter in BASIC...

10 FOR N = 1 TO 10
20 LPRINT "TESTING ";N
30 NEXT N

 ...does it print OK?
                        Brian

From Miles Kinloch, EDINBURGH


Dear Brian,

Many thanks for another great
issue of OUTLET - well done once
again! I like the way you've
presented SNAPFIX and BLOCKMAKER
-the animation in the title page
for the latter looks excellent.

However,  I have to draw your
attention to a couple of small
editing errors that seem to have
crept in...

With SNAPFIX, it's happened as a
result of combining the Betados
and G+Dos versions into one pro-
gram...


When you select the G+Dos option
it reads the DATA lines for Beta
Dos because the RESTORE command
in line 270 should be RESTORE
4000. Thankfully, the DATA is
not 'POKEd @' directly into the
DOS but set up in Spectrum RAM
first. As a result, the worst
scenario, ie, that of someone
inadvertently corrupting their
DOS, is avoided. What it does
do, at least in my case, is
cause the program to be LISTed!

No doubt this will probably
cause a few raised eyebrows but
at least there's no real harm
done. (The Betados option works
OK of course since the DATA
lines for it are the first ones
in the program.)


The problem with BLOCKMAKER
concerns the variables 'l' and
'c' in line 10, ie, the default
values when the program is RUN.
I had set these both to 0 (ie,
the top left-hand corner of
screen) to cater for the largest
possible frame size, ie, a full
screen. However, I notice you've
changed them to 7 and 12 resp-
ectively. While this is fine
for the demo sequence of frames
there would be a problem if the
currently-stored sequence happ-
ened to contain any frame that
was too large to fit at position
7,12. The result would be a
'parameter error' if the program
were stopped and re-RUN, ie,
either through pressing Symbol
Shift/A or through a disk error.


If you could therefore maybe ask
people to change these to LET
l=0 : LET c=0 and resave the
program, that will sort it.

Anyway, sorry to be a moan but I
thought I'd better mention these
things!

          Best wishes,

         Miles Kinloch

Brian Cavers to Miles Kinloch

Thanks, Miles.

I think originally I felt that
the default frame position and
size in BLOCKMAKER was rather
tedious to keep moving - ie that
it would be better to start in
the centre and be fairly small.
That way, on average, it would
be at the minimum distance from
where you want to move it!

By the way, has everyone noticed
that rotating frame on the title
page incorporates an optical
illusion? It can look like you
are looking UP at say, a space
station - OR looking DOWN at a
revolving dish!


I always see it first as though
I am looking UP at from beneath
and it takes some concentration
for a minute or so before I see
it from the other viewpoint. I
have NEVER yet it seen from
ABOVE at FIRST glance. I wonder
why that is? Has anybody else
seen this?
                         Brian

From Malcolm Goodman, LEEDS

Dear Brian/Ron,

In Issue 96 you published 'Prog-
stopper' as a means of removing
the auto run from a BASIC pro-
gram on the Disciple/+D.  This
assumes of course that the MERGE
command doesn't work because of
some protection that has been
included. However,if you LOAD Pn
and then keep your finger on the
BREAK key when the disc drive
whirls, the autorun will be
defeated and the program will be
at your mercy.

                Malcolm Goodman

Brian Cavers to Malcolm Goodman

Mmmm... Seems too easy! However,
I tried it and can't think why I
didn't realize this before. I
guess that it is a hangover from
other systems where, if you use
BREAK while a file is loading it
aborts the load. The +D doesn't
seem to do this but disables
BREAK while loading. Nice tip!

                      Brian


From George Munro, LONDON, NW3.

Dear Ron,

I regret to have to tell you
that in the Program "TITLEMAKER"
[OUTLET 96 +D version only - Ed]
someone changed line 365 to read
"CODE 64000" instead of "CODE
62000" and LINE 376 to read
"POKE VAL w$,VAL 249" which
previously had read, " POKE VAL
w$, VAL "241":POKE VAL v$,VAL
"48"."

I appreciate that someone had
perhaps been trying to save
"bytes", and had felt that it
did not matter where the new
typeface was to be located in
memory.


One would have thought that the
program would have worked with
this change but unfortunately
such is not the case. If you try
to change back and forward
between typefaces it just does
not work.

Why this should be so I do not
quite understand.  I have
"LLISTED" the program and
searched it from end to end but
to no avail. Since I am only a
beginner in this programming
business, perhaps some more ex-
pert soul may be able to provide
a solution.

I wonder if it could be a clash
of machine CODE as to where the
GOSUBs are loaded?


At any rate, to make it work one
needs to alter LINE 365 to read
"LOAD d*;T$CODE VAL "62000" and
LINE 376 to read "GO SUB arr:
POKE VAL w$,VAL"241":POKE VAL
v$,VAL "48"

Since the whole purpose of ITEM
6. "RETURN OLD TYPEFACE", and
ITEM 7."REGAIN NEW TYPEFACE" is
to swap and change typefaces, I
feel that without my suggested
correction then the program
loses much of its usefulness.

Regards to all involved with
OUTLET, keep up the good work.

           Yours Aye,

        George B. Munro


Brian Cavers to George Munro

Sorry George but for once I do
not think this is our fault. As
I receive contributed programs I
copy them to a disk unaltered
and then send a copy to Chris
Oliver, our programs editor. I
checked the original program you
sent us in March and the error
was in the original!

I can see no reason why I would
have made any such change as you
describe anyway - it makes no
sense and at that point I would
not have interfered with it.

Whatever the cause, all that
matters is that you have sent us
the cure which readers can use.
Thanks, George.       Brian

From Ronald Raaijen, HOLLAND



Hello Brian & Ron,

I have to think the Spectrum is
seriously dead in the UK. Lucky
there's a massive strong popula-
tion of serious users over here
in West Europe and east Europe.
I've made a good contact in the
Czech Republic with a Spectrum
computer group. On my holiday
next week I hope to visit them,
and also I will look again in
Romania for users.


Keep up the good work in both
areas of computing.


Is it possible to connect Spect-
rum Outlets to PC Emulator tape
files (not single files) so we
can store all OUTLETs on a hard
disk as a tape program?

Did the OUTLET Spectrum for the
Opus differ from Nos. 1 to 96
for the +D?? And can they still
be bought?

Is there already a Spectrum
software list on a database PC?
I'm working on one on my PC -
I've 4500 entries and I've
started to control, add, edit
from 1993 on now. Pete Fountain
(Sinclair Classics) was
interested - is somebody else?

       Keep on Computing,
             Ronald Raaijen

Brian Cavers to Ronald Raaijen

It should be possible to run the
Spectrum OUTLETs as an emulator
tape file but it might be a bit
laborious converting them. You'd
need to load each file, alter
the LOAD syntax to tape and SAVE
it to tape. The main areas to
look at are line 50 in the auto-
load file, around 1000 in the
CONTENTS BASIC, and lines 8915
to 8930 in individual programs.
You need also to be alert to any
code loaded.

However, it may be possible to
automate all this. If you just
load each program, BREAK and
RUN 9983 to save it to the tape
file it may be possible to alter
the syntax this way...

Write a simple BASIC routine to
OPEN the finished TAP file and
scan through for the +D syntax
D* and replace with two spaces.
If Opus then I think I used the
microdrive syntax LOAD "M";1; so
you would need to replace that
with six spaces.

You also need to find the length
of the code files and save them
all manually.

Apart from the disk syntax and
things like the autoload file
being called "run", The Opus
version of OUTLET only differed
from the +D in that it did not
have room for ADDENDERS. There
may have been the occasional
program that was different such
as CATLOADER.

I do not know of any Spectrum
software list on the PC. Is this
intended to be a definitive list
of ALL known Spectrum software?

                        Brian.

From: Peter Deane, BRIGHTON

Dear Ron,

I notice that you have dropped
the Opus print out option.  Can
you give me details of how to
puut it back in as I still have
not been able to get a Disciple
drive yet.

         All the best,

             Peter

Brian Cavers to Peter Deane

Sorry Peter, I forgot that there
were still one or two people who
convert the Disciple version to
Opus.

In the CONTENTS BASIC change the
line 1379 to...

1379 CLEAR # : OPEN #3;"B":
     LPRINT E$;"@": LET P$="O":
     RETURN

                     Brian.

### От: Miles Kinloch, EDINBURGH

Тем не менее, я должен обратить ваше внимание на пару небольших ошибок редактирования, которые, похоже, закрались в номер...

В SNAPFIX это произошло из-за объединения версий для Betados и G+Dos в одну программу...

Когда вы выбираете вариант G+Dos, программа читает строки DATA для Beta Dos, потому что команда RESTORE в строке 270 должна быть `RESTORE 4000`. К счастью, эти DATA не заносятся напрямую через 'POKE @' в DOS, а сначала подготавливаются в оперативной памяти Спектрума. В результате худшего сценария — случайного повреждения DOS — удается избежать. Но к чему это приводит (по крайней мере, в моем случае), так это к выводу листинга программы через LIST!

Без сомнения, это вызовет у кого-то недоумение, но, по крайней мере, реального вреда не нанесено. (Вариант с Betados, конечно же, работает отлично, поскольку строки DATA для него идут в программе первыми).

Проблема с BLOCKMAKER касается переменных 'l' и 'c' в строке 10, то есть значений по умолчанию при запуске программы по RUN. Я установил их обе в 0 (то есть в верхний левый угол экрана), чтобы учесть максимально возможный размер фрейма — полный экран. Однако я заметил, что вы изменили их на 7 и 12 соответственно. Хотя для демонстрационной последовательности кадров это подходит, возникнет проблема, если в текущей сохраненной последовательности окажется фрейм, который слишком велик, чтобы поместиться в позиции 7,12. Результатом будет 'parameter error', если программа будет остановлена и перезапущена по RUN — будь то через нажатие Symbol Shift/A или из-за ошибки диска.

Поэтому, если вы могли бы попросить читателей изменить их обратно на `LET l=0 : LET c=0` и пересохранить программу, проблема решится.

В любом случае, извините за ворчание, но я счел своим долгом упомянуть об этих вещах!

С наилучшими пожеланиями,  
Miles Kinloch

### Brian Cavers — Ronald Raaijen

Запустить Spectrum OUTLET в виде ленточного файла для эмулятора вполне возможно, но их конвертация может оказаться довольно трудоёмкой. Придётся загружать каждый файл, менять синтаксис команды LOAD на ленточный и сохранять (SAVE) его на ленту. Основные места, на которые стоит обратить внимание: строка 50 в файле автозагрузки, в районе строки 1000 в CONTENTS BASIC и строки с 8915 по 8930 в отдельных программах. Также нужно быть внимательным ко всем загружаемым кодовым блокам.

Впрочем, возможно, всё это удастся автоматизировать. Если просто загружать каждую программу, нажимать BREAK и делать `RUN 9983`, чтобы сохранить её в файл ленты, то изменить синтаксис можно следующим образом...

Напишите простую Бейсик-процедуру, которая открывает (OPEN) готовый TAP-файл, ищет синтаксис +D `D*` и заменяет его двумя пробелами. Если это версия для Opus, то там, кажется, использовался синтаксис микродрайва `LOAD "M";1;`, так что его нужно будет заменить шестью пробелами.

Вам также понадобится узнать длину кодовых файлов и сохранить их все вручную.

Если не считать дискового синтаксиса и того, что автозагрузочный файл назывался «run», версия OUTLET для Opus отличалась от версии для +D лишь тем, что на ней не оставалось места для рубрики ADDENDERS. Изредка могли отличаться отдельные утилиты, такие как CATLOADER.
